title: Rename 'account re-auth' → 'account refresh'
description: Rename the 'account re-auth' command to 'account refresh'. The current name 're-auth' is jargon-heavy and non-standard. 'refresh' clearly communicates that it refreshes an existing account's OAuth tokens using the stored configuration. Keep 'account re-auth' as a deprecated alias.
prerequisiteState: Stories 1–27 complete. Command is registered as 'account re-auth'. Deprecation infrastructure available.
goal: After this story: 'zapi account refresh' works identically to old 'zapi account re-auth'. 'zapi account re-auth' still works but prints a deprecation warning. All flags (--name, --email, --zuidstring) and output format unchanged.
scope: In src/ZapiCli/Commands/AccountCommands.cs: rename the class 'AccountReAuthCommand' → 'AccountRefreshCommand'. Rename 'AccountReAuthSettings' → 'AccountRefreshSettings'. Update all internal references.

Register a deprecated shim: create 'AccountReAuthDeprecatedCommand' that subclasses AccountRefreshCommand and calls DeprecationHelper.Warn("account re-auth", "account refresh") in ExecuteAsync before calling base. Register under config.AddCommand<AccountReAuthDeprecatedCommand>("re-auth") inside the account branch.
Do NOT change any flags (--name, --email, --zuidstring) or output format ({ status: ok, data: { name: '...' } }) or error codes.
acceptanceCriteria: 'zapi account refresh --name myaccount' re-authenticates the account and prints the expected JSON
'zapi account re-auth --name myaccount' still works and prints a deprecation warning to stderr
Flags --name, --email, --zuidstring all work on both the new and deprecated names
All existing tests pass (update AccountReAuthCommand references to AccountRefreshCommand)
contextForAgent: This is a straightforward rename following the same pattern as story 28. Read AccountReAuthCommand in AccountCommands.cs first. The class rename is the primary concern — ensure no test file or service still imports 'AccountReAuthCommand' after the rename.
